ثَيْتَلٌ The وَعِل [or mountain-goat], (M, K,) as a general term: (M:) [in the present day, but vulgarly pronounced تَيْتَل, applied to the wild goat of the Arabian and Egyptian deserts and mountains; the capra jaela of Hamilton Smith; called by some an ibex; as is also بَدَن:] or an old وعل: (S, M, Mgh, K:) or the male of the أَرْوَى: (Sh, T, M, K: [this is the same as the first explanation:]) En-Nadr says that it has small horns: (T:) Aboo-Kheyreh, that it is of the وُعُول, does not quit the mountain, and its horns have branches: (T, Mgh: *) he says that the وعول are dusky, or dingy, or of a hue inclining to black and dust-colour, with whiteness in their lower parts; and the ثَيَاتِل [pl. of ثَيْتَل] are like them in their colours, and only distinguished from them by the horns; the وعل having long horns, which extend backwards until they meet over his tail: (T:) also a species of [the bovine antelope called] بَقَرُ الوَحْشِ, (M, K,) that abides in the mountains. (M.) ―
-b2- A man who sits with women. (TA.) ―
-b3- Incapable of going in to women; or not desirous of women. (K.) ―
-b4- A bulky, or corpulent, man, in whom one thinks there is good (AA, K, TA) when there is no good in him: (AA, TA:) but, as mentioned by As, it is تيتل. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
